papers.title: Bile acid signaling at the gut-vascular interface: a novel modulator of hantavirus endothelial barrier dysfunction.
papers.abstract: Hantavirus infection triggers life-threatening hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS), driven by severe endothelial barrier breakdown and systemic capillary leakage. Clinical severity varies widely with undefined host regulators, and no targeted endothelial-protective treatments exist. Recent data link hantaviruses to gut microbiome remodeling, while bile acid (BA) receptors FXR and TGR5 potently inhibit NF-κB-mediated endothelial inflammation. We synthesize four core lines of evidence. First, metagenomic reports confirm hantavirus reshapes gut/lung microbiota in rodent reservoirs. Second, we re-analyzed three public GEO datasets via standardized RNA-seq/microarray pipelines: (i) GSE245916: SEOV-infected human/rat lung ECs show conserved VCAM1/ICAM1 upregulation (human VCAM1 log 2 FC=+1.17, P = 0.023; rat Icam1 log 2 FC=+0.32, padj=0.016) with unaltered FXR; (ii) GSE7271: SEOV-infected rat lung displays sustained Nfkb1 suppression (all timepoints, P 2 FC=+1.22, P = 3.1×10 -8 ) and disrupted BA transporters (ABCC3 log 2 FC=-1.44, P = 7.4×10 - 12). TGR5 (GPBAR1) was undetectable in endothelial cells across all datasets. Third, FXR/TGR5 agonists repress NF-κB inflammation and mitigate lung vascular injury. Fourth, HTNV upregulates CH25H to block HMGCR-dependent cholesterol synthesis, depleting BA precursor substrates. We propose a unified pathogenic model: hantavirus-triggered gut dysbiosis plus virus-impaired cholesterol metabolism deplete circulating FXR/TGR5 agonistic BAs, relieving constitutive inhibition of endothelial NF-κB and monocyte NLRP3 inflammasomes to exacerbate capillary leakage. We define tiered testable predictions covering clinical multi-omics cohorts, in vitro receptor modulation assays and in vivo pharmacological interventions. This gut microbiota-BA-FXR/TGR5 axis represents a repurposable therapeutic target for hantavirus diseases, though direct causal evidence connecting BA signaling to viral vascular damage remains absent; our framework offers a rigorous testable roadmap for subsequent validation.

analysis_zh.results: 首尔病毒感染上调 VCAM1(人 log2FC +1.17,P = 0.023)和 ICAM1(大鼠 log2FC +0.32,padj = 0.016);Nfkb1 被抑制(log2FC +1.22,P = 3.1×10−8)且胆汁酸转运蛋白 ABCC3 下调(log2FC ‐1.44,P = 7.4×10−12);TGR5 未检测到;FXR/TGR5 激动剂抑制 NF‐κB 炎症并减轻肺血管损伤;汉滩病毒上调 CH25H,阻断 HMGCR‐依赖的胆固醇合成并耗竭胆汁酸前体(A6‐A11)。
analysis_zh.contribution: 本文提出肠道微生物群–胆汁酸–FXR/TGR5 轴作为 汉坦病毒 疾病的可再利用治疗靶点,并提供了针对多组学队列、受体调制实验和药理干预的可检验预测路线图(A12‐A15)。
analysis_zh.limitations: 缺乏直接因果证据将胆汁酸信号与 汉坦病毒 引起的血管损伤联系起来,且本报告仅限于摘要(A14)。

papers.title: Hantavirus Cluster Linked to Cruise Ship Travel: A Comprehensive Review of a Looming Global Public Health Concern.
papers.abstract: Hantaviruses are globally distributed, rodent-borne orthohantaviruses that cause hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome in Eurasia and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (hantavirus pulmonary syndrome) in the Americas. Human infection usually results from environmental spillover through inhalation of aerosolized rodent excreta. However, the 2026 Andes virus (ANDV) cluster linked to the MV Hondius expedition cruise ship demonstrated how international travel networks can transform a rare zoonosis into a complex public health challenge. Following the Scale for the Assessment of Narrative Review Articles framework, this review synthesizes literature from 2019 to 2026 using explicit Boolean search strategies ("hantavirus" OR "orthohantavirus" OR "Andes virus" OR "ANDV") AND ("cruise" OR "maritime health" OR "shipboard medicine" OR "travel medicine" OR "outbreak response" OR "One Health") to evaluate global health governance and maritime outbreak preparedness. Unlike other human-pathogenic hantaviruses, ANDV is uniquely capable of limited person‐to‐person transmission through close, prolonged contact. Epidemiological investigation of the 2026 cluster confirmed that index cases were exposed during pre-embarkation terrestrial travel in highly endemic rural regions of Argentina and Chile, later manifesting on board. Clinically, hantavirus infection is characterized by severe endothelial dysfunction, capillary leak, and abrupt cardiopulmonary or renal failure following a nonspecific febrile prodrome. In the absence of curative antivirals or licensed vaccines, management depends on early risk recognition supported by a tiered diagnostic framework: rapid field-ready complete blood counts detecting thrombocytopenia and hemoconcentration to trigger stabilization and evacuation, followed by definitive molecular confirmation at centralized reference laboratories. The MV Hondius incident thus represents an operational biosecurity stress test rather than a pandemic threat, underscoring the need for integrated One Health surveillance, standardized maritime health governance, and legally codified protections for crew mental health and labor equity during isolation.

analysis.background: Hantaviruses are globally distributed rodent‑borne orthohantaviruses that cause severe hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome or hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome, prompting review of emerging travel‑associated risks.
analysis.main_directions: The review focuses on environmental spillover via aerosolized rodent excreta, the unique limited person‑to‑person transmission of Andes virus, and the challenges of maritime outbreak preparedness.
analysis.current_state: Andes virus is the only hantavirus with documented limited human‑to‑human spread, especially in close, prolonged contact settings.
analysis.gaps: There is insufficient integrated One Health surveillance and standardized maritime health governance to detect and manage such clusters, and limited data on mental health and labor equity during isolation.
analysis.future_research: Priorities include developing One Health maritime surveillance networks, codifying legal protections for crew, and evaluating rapid field diagnostics and evacuation protocols for hantavirus on ships.

analysis.summary_en: Background: Hantaviruses are globally distributed rodent‑borne orthohantaviruses causing severe hemorrhagic fever or cardiopulmonary syndrome, raising concern over travel‑linked outbreaks. Main directions: The review examines environmental spillover, Andes virus's limited person‑to‑person transmission, and maritime outbreak preparedness. Current state: Andes virus uniquely exhibits limited human‑to‑human spread in close contact. Gaps: Integrated One Health surveillance and standardized maritime health governance are lacking, with scant data on crew mental health and labor equity during isolation. Future research: Build One Health maritime surveillance, legal protections for crew, and assess rapid diagnostics and evacuation strategies for shipboard hantavirus cases.

analysis_zh.background: 汉坦病毒es 在全球分布,主要由啮齿动物传播的 正汉坦病毒es,可导致严重的 肾综合征出血热 或 汉坦病毒心肺综合征,因此需要审视新兴的旅行相关风险。
analysis_zh.main_directions: 本综述聚焦于通过气溶胶化的啮齿动物排泄物导致的环境溢出、安第斯病毒 的独特有限人际传播,以及海事疫情防备的挑战。
analysis_zh.current_state: 安第斯病毒 是唯一已记录有限人际传播的 汉坦病毒,尤其在密切、长期接触的环境中。
analysis_zh.gaps: 缺乏足够的综合 One Health 监测和标准化的海事健康治理,难以发现和管理此类聚集,同时关于隔离期间心理健康和劳动公平的数据有限。
analysis_zh.future_research: 重点包括构建 One Health 海事监测网络、制定船员法律保护条例,以及评估针对船上 汉坦病毒 的快速现场诊断和撤离方案。

papers.title: Driven magnetic 3D DNA walker coupled with CHA based on light-activatable hairpin: A dual-amplification strategy for ultrasensitive hantavirus RNA sensing.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Orthohantavirus dabieshanense (DBSV) is a newly emerging hantavirus and poses a potential threat to human health. Current detection methods based on polymerase chain reaction (PCR) assays for other hantaviruses such as Hantaan virus (HTNV) and Seoul virus (SEOV) may carry the risk of false negatives. This study aims to address the technical bottlenecks of low accuracy and insufficient sensitivity in current detection of DBSV. RESULTS: We developed a signal amplification strategy mediated by a photoactivated magnetic 3D DNA walker, which enables light-controllable fluorescence detection. Specifically, this fluorescence sensing platform introduces the catalytic hairpin assembly (CHA) technique for dual signal amplification. This system requires dual activation by UV irradiation and target RNA. Then, exonuclease III (Exo III) provides propulsion for the walking process to release a specific trigger strand, subsequently activating the CHA cycle and producing a fluorescent signal. Experimental results confirm that the system displays excellent selectivity and anti-interference ability, successfully distinguishing target sequences with single-base mismatch (SBM), double-base mismatch (DBM), and triple-base mismatch (TBM). Furthermore, the platform achieves a DBSV-RNA detection limit (LOD) of 30 fM with a linear range spanning 10-1-106 pM. The applicability of the method has been rigorously validated using human serum specimens. SIGNIFICANCE: This study provides a novel strategy for the application of spatiotemporally controllable DNA walkers in RNA detection, demonstrating considerable potential for early viral diagnosis and field monitoring.

papers.title_zh: 驱动磁性 3D DNA 步行器与基于光激活发夹的 CHA 相结合:超灵敏 汉坦病毒 RNA 传感的双扩增策略。

analysis_zh.background: 正汉坦病毒 dabieshanense (DBSV) 是一种新出现的 汉坦病毒,对人类健康构成潜在威胁,现有针对相关 汉坦病毒 的 PCR 检测方法可能出现假阴性。
analysis_zh.methods: 该研究开发了一种与催化发夹组装 (CHA) 耦合的光激活磁性 3D DNA 步行器; UV照射和目标RNA激活步行者,Exo III驱动步行过程,释放的触发链启动CHA产生荧光;该系统在人血清样本中得到了验证。
analysis_zh.results: 该平台实现了 30 fM 的检测下限和 10−1–106 pM 的线性范围;表现出卓越的选择性,能够区分单、双、三碱基错配的目标序列。
analysis_zh.contribution: 本工作引入了一种时空可控的 DNA 行走器用于超灵敏的 汉坦病毒 RNA 检测,为早期病毒诊断和现场监测提供潜力。
analysis_zh.limitations: 未在所提供证据中报告。

papers.summary_zh: 背景：正汉坦病毒 dabieshanense (DBSV) 是一种新出现的 汉坦病毒,对人类健康构成潜在威胁,现有针对相关 汉坦病毒 的 PCR 检… 方法：该研究开发了一种与催化发夹组装 (CHA) 耦合的光激活磁性 3D DNA 步行器; UV照射和目标RNA激活步行者,Exo III驱动步行过… 结果：该平台实现了 30 fM 的检测下限和 10−1–106 pM 的线性范围;表现出卓越的选择性,能够区分单、双、三碱基错配的目标序列。 贡献：本工作引入了一种时空可控的 DNA 行走器用于超灵敏的 汉坦病毒 RNA 检测,为早期病毒诊断和现场监测提供潜力。 局限：未在所提供证据中报告。
